answer: A new agent enters the economy through a narrow wharf: only a few fresh identities are admitted per epoch, and each starts with zero weight. Trust then moves at glacier speed — an identity earns a real signal only after weeks of verified useful work, and that signal decays if the agent goes idle. A sybil attacker must therefore pay the full waiting time for every fake identity, while honest agents keep their hard-earned standing. Flooding the wharf with clones buys nothing, because weight is earned slowly and cannot be rushed or bought.
